<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|CHA. XIX.|OF THE APOSTLES.|347}}</noinclude>{{verse|chapter=18|verse=23}}† And hauing taried there a certaine time, he departed, vvalking in order through the countrie of Galatia and Phrygia, confirming al the disciples.

{{verse|chapter=18|verse=24}}† And a certaine Iew, named {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ Apollo.}}∷ Apollo, borne at Alexandria, an eloquent man, came to Ephesus, mighty in the scriptures. {{verse|chapter=18|verse=25}}† This man was taught the vvay of our Lord: and being feruent in spirit he spake, and taught diligently those things that pertaine to {{sc|Iesvs}}, knovving only the baptisme of Iohn. {{verse|chapter=18|verse=26}}† This man therfore began to deale confidently in the synagogue. Vvhom vvhen Priscilla and Aquila had heard, they tooke him vnto them, and expounded to him the vvay of our Lord more diligently. {{verse|chapter=18|verse=27}}† And vvhereas he vvas desirous to goe to Achaia, the brethren exhorting vvrote to the disciples to receiue him. Vvho, vvhen he vvas come, profited them much that had beleeued. {{verse|chapter=18|verse=28}}† For he vvith vehemencie conuinced the Iewes openly, shewing by the scriptures, that {{sc|Iesvs}} is {{sc|Christ}}.

{{c|{{larger|{{sc|Chap. XIX.}}}}}}

{{c|''How Paul began the Church of Ephesus, first in 12 that vvere baptized with Iohns baptisme, 8 then preaching three moneths in the Synagogue of the Iewes, vntil for their obstinacie and blaspheming, he forsooke them, disputing afterward in a certaine schoole for two yeres space to the maruelous increase of the Church, specially through his great miracles also, in healing diseases with the touche of his clothes, and expelling diuels, 13 vvho yet contemned the Exorcists of the Iewes. 18 How the Christians there confesse their actes, and burne their vnlawful bookes: 21 and how he foretold that after he had been at Hierusalem, he must see Rome. 23 and what a great sedition vvas raised against him at Ephesus, by them that got their liuing of vvorking to the idolatrous Temple of Diana.''}} {{dropinitial|A|image=Rhemes New Testament 1582 initial A, two satyrs.png|imgsize=185px|fl={{verse|chapter=19|verse=1}}}}ND {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=The Epistle vpō Whitson-eue.}}it came to passe vvhen Apollo vvas at Corinth, that Paul hauing gone through the higher partes came to Ephesus, and found certaine disciples: {{verse|chapter=19|verse=2}}† and he said to them, Haue you receiued the holy Ghost, beleeuing? But they said to him, Nay, neither haue vve heard Whether there be a holy Ghost. {{verse|chapter=19|verse=3}}† But he said, In vvhat then vvere you baptized? Vvho said, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ Iohns Baptism not sufficient.}}∷ In Iohns baptisme. {{verse|chapter=19|verse=4}}† And Paul said: {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 3, 11. Mr. 1, 8. Lu. 3, 16.''}}* Iohn baptized the people vvith the baptisme of penance, saying: That they should beleeue in him that vvas to come after him, that is to say, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ Christs Baptism necessarie.}}∷ in {{sc|Iesvs}}. {{verse|chapter=19|verse=5}}† Hearing these things, they vvere baptized in the name of our Lord {{sc|Iesvs}}.<noinclude>{{rh||Xx ij|And}}</noinclude>
